dedupe_keys.name: egrid emissions generation resource integrated database us epa emissions generation and resource mix for almost all us power plants

description: eGRID, the Emissions & Generation Resource Integrated Database, is the US Environmental Protection Agency source of data on the environmental characteristics of almost all electric power generated in the United States. It gives emissions, emission rates, generation, heat input and resource mix, with information identifying power plants, their attributes and location. Data are provided separately at combustion unit and generator level, combined at plant level, and aggregated to state, US total and three sets of grid regions: balancing authority area, NERC region and eGRID subregion. The latest edition, eGRID2023, is the eighteenth, released in January 2025 with 2023 data and revised on 17 January and 12 June 2025; since eGRID2012 it includes every plant and generator, including plants with zero generation. Current editions are available online as an Excel download with a technical guide, metric file and release notes, and a historical ZIP holds editions from 1996 to 2016; subregion shapefiles are provided. The EPA states the data are public domain and may be used commercially. Coverage is the United States, including Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico. Caveats: the latest data year is 2023 and a few plants have generation by fuel type that does not sum to the plant total. Simulation uses are a plant-level US generation fleet with locations and emission rates for capacity expansion, dispatch and exposure studies. Related records: data-epa-power-plants-neighboring-communities builds on eGRID; data-eia-860-annual-electric-generator-report is the EIA generator inventory.
